summary: Eleven comment-endorsed security, networking, AI, systems, focus, and learning tools from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: ruby-landlock
items.source_story_title: A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repos
items.summary: A Ruby gem that confines external binaries with Linux Landlock sandboxes.
items.why_included: Two production users recommended it for defense-in-depth around native image-processing tools.
items.evidence: Discourse runs external binaries inside ruby-landlock, while another user applies it to image processing.

evidence_sources.author: sams99
evidence_sources.excerpt: we now run all external binaries, including magick via a landlock sandbox.

evidence_sources.author: kawsper
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use ruby-landlock as well for image processing.

items.name: Pangolin
items.summary: A self-hosted reverse proxy and VPN for public or authenticated private resources.
items.why_included: Two homelab users praised its long-term reliability and user experience.
items.evidence: One user called Pangolin great after extended use; another preferred its UX to NetBird.

evidence_sources.author: tamimio
evidence_sources.excerpt: Use pangolin (you can self host), been using it for a while and it’s great

items.name: OpenZiti
items.summary: An open-source zero-trust overlay for identity-gated, otherwise invisible network services.
items.why_included: A self-hoster praised its granular access controls and dark-service routing.
items.evidence: The commenter enjoyed OpenZiti and called its granular private-service controls a game changer.

evidence_sources.author: gibs0ns
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have really enjoyed the experience of OpenZiti for this purpose.

items.name: Mercury 2.5
items.summary: Inception's low-latency diffusion language model for fast production reasoning.
items.why_included: A commenter called it groundbreaking and explicitly recommended trying it.
items.evidence: The recommendation singled out Mercury 2.5 as a diffusion model worth trying.

evidence_sources.author: Topfi
evidence_sources.excerpt: Mercury 2.5 is truly groundbreaking, giving it a try is highly recommended.

items.name: CostGoat
items.summary: A comparison site for checking LLM API prices and model costs.
items.why_included: A commenter uses it specifically to minimize model spending.
items.evidence: The commenter described CostGoat as their practical tool for finding cheaper LLM APIs.

evidence_sources.author: deedree
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use costgoat to be a cheapass

items.name: Jemalloc
items.summary: A general-purpose allocator with profiling, memory controls, and per-thread counters.
items.why_included: Users reported lower Rails memory use and useful per-thread workload budgeting.
items.evidence: One production user reported drastic Rails memory savings; another relies on per-thread allocation counters.

evidence_sources.author: collimarco
evidence_sources.excerpt: Jemalloc is great for Ruby on Rails apps, and drastically reduces memory usage for the same workloads.

evidence_sources.author: atombender
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Jemalloc on a project because it has per-thread allocation counters.

items.name: FEX
items.summary: A fast x86 and x86-64 userspace emulator for ARM64 Linux systems.
items.why_included: An ARM-handheld user praised its compatibility and battery-friendly results.
items.evidence: The commenter runs FEX on several ARM handhelds and called the project amazing.

evidence_sources.author: sureglymop
evidence_sources.excerpt: this project (FEX) is amazing. I've been running Armada OS on multiple ARM handhelds

items.name: Foqos
items.summary: A free open-source iPhone app blocker activated by NFC, QR, or barcodes.
items.why_included: A user strongly recommended it after cutting measured weekly screen time below one hour.
items.evidence: The commenter credited Foqos with very low weekly iPhone screen time and strongly recommended it.

evidence_sources.author: olwmc
evidence_sources.excerpt: if you're struggling with apps on your (i)phone, I can't recommend

items.name: Olauncher
items.summary: A minimalist keyboard-oriented Android launcher designed to reduce visual distraction.
items.why_included: A long-term launcher user said Olauncher had lasted the longest.
items.evidence: The commenter likes keyboard-based launchers and has retained Olauncher longer than alternatives.

items.name: Undefined Behavior: What Happened to My Code?
items.source_story_title: C++26: Trivial infinite loops are no longer undefined behaviour
items.summary: An article explaining why undefined behavior exists and where C and C++ overuse it.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommended it as a nuanced explanation of undefined behavior.
items.evidence: The recommendation praised the article's distinction between necessary and poorly chosen undefined behavior.

evidence_sources.author: ameliaquining
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend this explanation of why UB is good and necessary

items.name: Analysis I by Terence Tao
items.source_story_title: I vibed a proof of Conway's conjecture
items.summary: A rigorous real-analysis textbook that builds mathematics methodically from first principles.
items.why_included: A commenter strongly recommended it and credited it with getting them into proofs.
items.evidence: The commenter found Tao's methodical foundation accessible and personally useful for learning proofs.

evidence_sources.author: danabramov
evidence_sources.excerpt: I highly recommend Terence Tao's Analysis textbook
